holdings.name: Salesforce
holdings.business: Salesforce sells cloud CRM and enterprise software for sales, service, marketing, and analytics worldwide.
holdings.reasoning: Enterprise CRM leader with sticky subscriptions — watch AI (Agentforce) attach rates and margin expansion versus cloud spend growth.

holdings.name: Urban Outfitters Inc
holdings.business: Urban Outfitters retails apparel and home goods through Urban Outfitters, Anthropologie, and Free People brands.
holdings.reasoning: Cheaper than peers at 14× earnings vs 30× median — cash flow jumped $97M → $445M; ~61% below our fair value.

holdings.name: IBM
holdings.business: IBM sells hybrid cloud, AI software, and IT consulting services to large enterprises worldwide.
holdings.reasoning: Software mix and consulting tied to hybrid cloud are lifting margins — the upgrade story is recurring software, not old hardware — profits up about 546%; cash flow up $10.0B → $11.6B; top-half growth (#5/12) in Information Technology Services.

holdings.name: Chewy
holdings.business: Chewy sells pet food, pharmacy, and supplies online to U.S. pet owners.
holdings.reasoning: Repeat Autoship orders and higher-margin own brands are lifting earnings as pet spending stays resilient — cash flow jumped $9M → $562M; profits up about 347%; top-half growth (#5/12) in Specialty Retail.

holdings.name: Boeing
holdings.business: Boeing designs and builds commercial airplanes, defense systems, and space vehicles.
holdings.reasoning: 737 MAX deliveries and defense cash are the recovery spine — hitting production targets is what rebuilds trust in Boeing's earnings.

holdings.name: Delta Air Lines
holdings.business: Delta Air Lines operates a U.S. network passenger airline with hubs in Atlanta, Detroit, Minneapolis, and New York.
holdings.reasoning: Premium seats and strong ticket prices are carrying Delta even as jet fuel jumps with oil — the brand is the ballast — cash flow jumped $16M → $3.8B; #2 growth rank of 6 in Airlines; profits up about 280%.

holdings.name: Tesla
holdings.business: Tesla designs and manufactures electric vehicles, energy storage, and solar products.
holdings.reasoning: Car volume, energy storage, and self-driving optionality remain the stacked story; near-term trading is about deliveries and margins — cash flow jumped $3.5B → $6.2B; #2 growth rank of 6 in Auto Manufacturers; profits down about 70%.
holdings.numbers: For me, this stock is impossible to hold short term - but I believe that it would be making history in the future world.

holdings.name: Fluor
holdings.business: Fluor provides engineering, procurement, and construction services for energy, infrastructure, and industrial projects worldwide.
holdings.reasoning: A big engineering backlog and energy-transition projects can support revenue for years if projects stay on track.

holdings.name: Halliburton
holdings.business: Halliburton provides oilfield services and equipment for drilling, completions, and production worldwide.
holdings.reasoning: When oil is high, oilfield work picks up; Halliburton's international mix helps if US fracking slows.

holdings.name: Incyte
holdings.business: Incyte discovers and commercializes oncology and inflammation medicines.
holdings.reasoning: Jakafi drug cash funds the pipeline while cancer-drug optionality keeps the biotech upside intact — cheaper than peers at 16× earnings vs 37× median; cash flow jumped $568M → $1.4B; ~73% below our fair value.

holdings.name: Comcast
holdings.business: Comcast provides cable broadband, wireless, and NBCUniversal media and streaming services.
holdings.reasoning: Broadband and NBCU cash fund the dividend while streaming losses narrow — cable customer loss is the risk, not the media assets — cheaper than peers at 5× earnings vs 10× median; ~78% below our fair value; profits up about 269%.
